Noah Rivera: hi team — Noah here, starting week 1. Trying to get my dev environment consistent across my M1 MacBook and a Linux VM. Hitting a few annoyances with asdf, dotfiles, and envrc. Quick list:

1) asdf installs OK but `asdf install go 1.20.6` fails with `openssl` not found when compiling from source
2) my bootstrap script symlinks dotfiles but ends up creating a weird ~/dotfiles/.git rather than bare repo setup
3) direnv doesn't pick up `export $(cat .env | xargs)` in .envrc — I get permission errors sometimes

Commands I ran:
```
brew install asdf openssl direnv
# clone dotfiles and run bootstrap script
git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/dotfiles.git ~/dotfiles
~/dotfiles/bootstrap.sh
asdf plugin-add golang
asdf install golang 1.20.6
```

Priya Nair (DevEx): welcome Noah! :wave: A few quick troubleshooting steps we suggest:
- OpenSSL: on mac you need to point builds to Homebrew OpenSSL. Try `export LDFLAGS=\"-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib\"` and `export CPPFLAGS=\"-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include\"` before `asdf install`. Also `brew link --force openssl@1.1` is sometimes needed (but prefer env vars).
- Dotfiles: we use a bare repo pattern. If your bootstrap created a nested repo, run the official script from our repo: `./scripts/setup-bare-repo.sh` which uses `git --git-dir=$HOME/.cfg --work-tree=$HOME`. Avoid cloning into ~/dotfiles unless the script expects it.
- direnv: permission issues are often from CRLF or from the file mode. Run `dos2unix .envrc` and `chmod 600 .envrc`, then `direnv allow`. For env parsing, prefer using `dotenv` helper: `dotenv -f .envrc .env` or in .envrc use `export $(cat .env | xargs -0)` only if safe.

Ethan Gomez: Also check your PATH order — asdf shims should come before system binaries. In bash/zsh add `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` and `export PATH=\"$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH\"`. If you switch between mac and linux, pin tool versions in the repo `.tool-versions` so asdf picks the same runtimes.

Noah Rivera: thanks everyone — setting the openssl flags fixed go install on mac. I re-ran the bootstrap script from the canonical repo and it created the bare config correctly. Converted .envrc to LF and direnv now allows. One small follow-up: is it OK to use zsh instead of fish? My shell differs between machines.

Priya Nair (DevEx): zsh is our standard and most docs assume it; fish can work but some bootstrap scripts are POSIX/sh oriented. If you prefer fish, we recommend installing `bass` or `fisher` helpers and sourcing the asdf shims as described in the onboarding doc. If it's easier, switch to zsh for a smoother experience. Ping me if you want us to pair and sync your shells. :+1:
